requests.title: Early country: radio, string bands and honky-tonk
requests.instructions: Investigate early and mid-century country performers, their actual stylistic role and documented links to Western swing, Honky-tonk, Folk, Bluegrass and later Nashville country. Distinguish influence from collaboration. Use Country Music Hall of Fame biographies or other institutional sources before any visible connection; Wikipedia links alone are only leads.
requests.notes: Country-roots first; only documented bridges to folk and rock.

requests.title: Country branches: Nashville, Bakersfield and songwriter tradition
requests.instructions: Research these artists as distinct country traditions, not one generic country cluster. Look for verified links to Bakersfield sound, Western swing, Honky-tonk, Outlaw country, folk songwriting and country-rock where the source explicitly supports them. Do not turn albums, labels, venues or television programs into nodes.
requests.notes: Keep era and regional differences legible; source each named relationship.

requests.title: Jazz foundations: swing, bebop and vocal lines
requests.instructions: Research jazz performers across swing, vocal jazz and bebop. Connect each to Jazz and a narrower style only when documented by NEA Jazz Masters, Library of Congress, Smithsonian or equivalent primary institution. Only claim band memberships or direct influence with specific evidence; avoid broad all-to-all jazz links.
requests.notes: Jazz zone: separate swing, bebop and vocal jazz paths.

requests.title: Jazz development: modal, free jazz and fusion
requests.instructions: Investigate the musicians around modal jazz, avant-garde jazz and jazz fusion. Verify the exact Miles Davis, John Coltrane and Herbie Hancock collaborations rather than assuming them from a shared scene. Keep chronology explicit and distinguish Cool jazz, Modal jazz, hard bop, free jazz and fusion. Use NEA and museum biographies as the connection basis.
requests.notes: Distinct musical developments, with cross-zone jazz-to-funk bridges only when sourced.

requests.title: Gospel, vocal R&B and early soul groups
requests.instructions: Research the difference between gospel groups, doo-wop, Motown and R&B vocal groups. Seek specific bridges to Gospel music, Rhythm and blues, Soul music and Pop music, backed by Rock Hall, Stax, Smithsonian or official museum evidence. Do not infer a shared label, producer or collaboration from a co-mention.
requests.notes: Gospel is not interchangeable with soul; identify the actual transition.

requests.title: Soul and funk lines into later popular music
requests.instructions: Research soul, funk and their documented influence on later pop, disco and hip-hop without inventing direct person-to-person relationships. Verify genre and group membership on institutional artist pages. Treat samples, recordings and labels as evidence; do not add them as standalone map nodes.
requests.notes: Bridge pop-soul-disco and hip-hop-rap only for historically documented reasons.
